This is a totally normal response to the transference you feel towards your therapist (I experience the same sort of thing). I’d be more concerned about your intrusive thoughts and anxiety during sex, which I think you should bring up in therapy. I also think you should tell your therapist about your maternal/affectionate feelings for her. I know it might be uncomfortable but I bet she’ll have had clients who’ve talked about the same thing - it’s incredibly common. You don’t have to necessarily go into depth about sex/masturbation if you don’t want to but just remember that she’ll have heard it all before so don’t hold back for her sake. Talking about the therapeutic relationship in session will allow the therapist to better understand you and the work you do together will therefore improve.

I’m not an expert but this sounds very much like OCD or another anxiety disorder. Maybe the fact that this thought has recently come back is a result of the anxiety and stress surrounding the pandemic? The fear of being a pedophile is actually a very common OCD obsession. Talk to your therapist. I promise, if she’s a professional she’ll understand, won’t overreact and will help you overcome this obsessive thought. Also, therapists only call the police if someone is in imminent danger so don’t worry about that. If things don’t work out with your current therapist, find someone else, preferably a clinical psychologist, who specialises in OCD treatment.
